entries.question: doc-kitty requires a guidance_text on every audience entry, and the current path-string audience carries none. What should the mechanical migration write?

entries.final_answer: external_references with a GitHub repository URL and the target's title, for every related entry that is not a published page (outside docs/, non-Markdown, draft, excluded). Frontmatter-only, so immutable bodies stay byte-identical, and no dead site link is added. A related entry whose target file no longer exists is dropped. Deviates from the issue's literal 'body link or drop'; flagged for the operator in the PR.
options: external_references with a GitHub repository URL (frontmatter-only)
entries.question: A published page's related entry that names a draft or excluded page is build-fatal. Move it into the body as a link, drop it, or move it to external_references as a repository URL?

entries.final_answer: Source-aware, mirroring the build: a published page's related names published pages only; a draft page's related may name drafts but no excluded page; an excluded page (never built, immutable history) keeps its related slugs to any existing page. Avoids rewriting 127 entries (105 in excluded history, 22 on drafts) into GitHub URLs for no build benefit. The corpus-shape test enforces the published rule, so when #6932 or an author publishes a draft, any related entry into a draft is named by the test. Autonomous-run default after review finding; flagged for the operator.
options: Source-aware: published source -> published targets only; draft source -> any non-excluded page; excluded source -> any page
Uniform: every unpublished target leaves related
entries.question: Which related targets must leave related? The spec said every unpublished target; doc-kitty only resolves related for pages it builds (an excluded page is never built; a draft is built only in a drafts-on preview, where drafts exist but excluded pages never do).
